articles.title: The Ravens have long been a model of stability. Now they’re going off the rails
articles.description: Baltimore have been one of the most successful teams in the league this century. But recent events have dinged their reputation The Baltimore Ravens have lost in all sorts of fashion in recent weeks. There were the blowout losses to juggernauts Buffalo, Jacksonville, and Cincinnati. There was the nailbiting divisional loss to Cleveland. There was the embarrassing defeat to the previously winless Chargers. But Sunday’s 35-33 loss to Carolina , the team’s sixth straight, hit different. Sunday was a massive test. Did Baltimore have the fortitude to bounce back and stay alive in the AFC North, with the hope of getting the injured Lamar Jackson back at some point? Almost. Continue reading...

articles.title: Gukesh vows to win world chess title ‘all over again’ as Sindarov challenge looms
articles.description: Youngest title match in chess history starts Tuesday Uzbek challenger enters as the oddsmakers’ favorite Champion plays down slump after falling to No 26 Read our World Chess Championship watch guide World chess champion Gukesh Dommaraju insisted he was approaching his first title defense with the mindset of a challenger on Sunday as he and Javokhir Sindarov faced the media ahead of their historic showdown in Geneva, the youngest matchup in the 140-year history of the sport’s most coveted title. The two 20-year-old grandmasters appeared side by side at the United Nations’ European headquarters in Geneva, where they struck a respectful tone before their best-of-14-games encounter begins on Tuesday at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, the affluent suburb overlooking Lake Geneva. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Haaland must be worried’: Thierno Barry’s rise has David Moyes purring
articles.description: Everton striker has worked hard to find his scoring touch after admitting he hit ‘rock bottom’ at times last season A most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. The rise of Thierno Barry may have surprised even the man himself but stands as a fitting reward for single-minded perseverance and the refusal to quit. “Fabulous” was David Moyes’s take on Barry’s last performance for Everton, when a double against Coventry took the striker to 10 goals for the season in all competitions and his team temporarily up to fifth. It was high praise indeed from a manager who does not dispense tributes freely, and can appear to be on the French forward’s case constantly, but was no more than Barry deserved for a display that also featured an assist for Everton’s third goal of the night. His six Premier League goals leave him joint third alongside Evanilson of Bournemouth and Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Music was our teacher’: the sound system pioneers reviving the scene in Manchester and beyond
articles.description: Manchester-based Megatone Sound Foundation and Baron Turbo Charge have rejuvenated the culture to offer a sense of belonging and empowerment For a generation of young Black Mancunians, some of the history lessons that mattered most were not taught in classrooms, but through towering stacks of amps and speakers, turntables and Jamaican records. “We didn’t know where we fit in. We didn’t know our history. Our parents were busy working two or three jobs,” says Errol “Barzy” Beaumont, a founder member of Baron Turbo Charge, Manchester’s long-running reggae sound system. “It was the records – Burning Spear, Bob Marley, Culture, that were telling us about our culture, which wasn’t on the school curriculum. For us, the sound system was not just entertainment – it was an education.” Continue reading...

articles.description: Amid the talk of Brighton being surprise title contenders this season, these are perhaps the afternoons which show the margin that still exists, and how the Premier League can provide the most punishing of wake-up calls at any moment. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. But for all the statement victories and the headline-grabbing moments , these games are the ones which can trip you up the most. Continue reading...

articles.description: Spaniard wins final 6-2, 7-6 (7) against new world No 1 Alcaraz the fourth to win career grand slam and ATP Finals The titles of ATP world No 1 and the best male tennis player in the world are carried by two different names. This has always been clear throughout this messy, injury-ravaged men’s season but it was underlined in the grand finale as Carlos Alcaraz ended his campaign with a statement victory, defeating the top-ranked player, Alexander Zverev, 6-2, 7-6 (7) to win the ATP Finals for the first time. So much of Alcaraz’s fortunes this season were defined by the wrist injury that forced him out for four and a half months during the spring and summer. articles.description: The head coach said he has watched videos from Eddie Jones’ time in charge to help England begin matches strongly Ellis Genge was so fired up by England’s powerful response to the haka on Saturday he stripped off his anthem jacket in the aftermath, completely forgetting he was not starting. Ollie Chessum told Lewis Moody, who had been invited to stand at the point of England’s V formation: “We are going long left, stay on the field and chase the kick-off.” And according to Ben Earl, who would still be out on the Twickenham turf carrying through traffic if he could, some players were so inspired by Moody’s speech the night before they could not sleep. Against that emotional backdrop, it is small wonder England flew out of the blocks against the All Blacks . Steve Borthwick has spoken a lot about “bringing the fire” recently and on Saturday they torched the place, riding the emotional wave that Moody’s presence inspired from Henry Slade’s fourth-minute try, through to a record victory against New Zealand . articles.title: 9/11 vets: Do politicians take the decision to go to war seriously?
articles.description: It is Veterans Day again, which means that, alongside the free red, white, and blue pancake specials and complimentary coffees, Americans will post tributes honoring the ultimate sacrifice of our soldiers. Just as predictably, on Memorial Day, veterans will receive well-intentioned messages thanking them for their service. Of course, Memorial Day honors those who died while serving in the U.S. military, whereas Veterans Day recognizes all who have served. This confusion is hardly something to get worked up about in itself. But it is symptomatic of something more consequential: a nation detached from its military and the wars it fights. In a sense, Americans are not wrong to conflate the two holidays. Service and sacrifice cannot be neatly separated, especially when the military has become an instrument of statecraft, diplomacy, humanitarian assistance, and lethal force whose deployment increasingly depends less on congressional authorization than on the decisions of a single president. Less than 1% of Americans serve in the military. articles.title: Are Democrats ready to make the most of the blue wave?
articles.description: Unless you’ve been living under a rock (no shame Patrick Star!), you’ve likely heard about last Tuesday’s “Blue Wave” midterm elections . The Democrats’ strong performance at the polls flipped control of the House and the Senate, delivering stunning results on the way, including flipping long-time red states like Kansas and Texas. As the GOP scrambles to repair the damage and Democrats strategize about how to use their new power in a divided Washington, one takeaway seems obvious: this was a foreign policy election, in which the Iran war and the costs it brought home served as the tipping point. But can we read these election results as a repudiation of U.S. foreign policy writ-large, or is this a specific response to one of the dumbest interventions in the long history of American adventurism? What does JD Vance's day-after effort to distance himself from the war tell us about how Republicans are digesting this result? And if Tuesday was a rebuke of U.S. foreign policy as usual, are Democrats ready to respond accordingly? articles.title: The Best Is Yet To Come Undone
articles.description: The Best Is Yet To Come Undone Submitted by QTR's Fringe Finance Today’s column is going to be two parts. First, I’m going to review a lot of what I’ve written about on this blog the last two weeks. Then, I’m going to offer my take on where Nvidia, the market, other sectors, and everything else is going forward. Punk band Lit had a great song called “The Best Is Yet To Come (Undone).” After Friday’s market crash and headlines suggesting that the SEC could be investigating Nvidia’s accounting, I can’t think of a more appropriate title for my column this weekend. Because if there’s one thing I’ve been trying to communicate to readers over the last four months, it’s that the unraveling of the AI bubble was never going to be a single event, a single bad earnings report, or a single afternoon of panic selling. It was going to be a chain reaction, one in which deteriorating sentiment, increasingly questionable financing arrangements, political uncertainty, and scrutiny of the companies at the center of the boom could begin feeding on one another. articles.title: Jeffrey Tucker: The Great Measles Scare, And Post-Pandemic Germophobia
articles.description: Jeffrey Tucker: The Great Measles Scare, And Post-Pandemic Germophobia Authored by Jeffrey A. Tucker via The Epoch Times , The period following a pandemic has usually been marked by a cultural germophobia. It's an irrational fear of infection. The tendency is to treat the air as dirty, people as disease vectors, and have inordinate fear of any sign of sickness. People are also more susceptible to believing any quack selling a potion as a preventive. This happened after 1918. The cultural panic over germs and infections did not stop for a generation. I'm not sure if the measles frenzy out there in the media now is sticking in the population, but the volume has become unbearably intense. For example, the whole of mainstream media has been screaming now for days about the supposed tragedy that the United States has lost its measles elimination status. Did you know that we had a measles elimination status? Maybe I did; I don't remember. This alone is a sign of propaganda, when you are told to be highly concerned and worried about something about which you knew nothing and never really cared. articles.title: ‘The platonic ideal of a wine glass’: we test the best for every budget
articles.description: Searching for a wine glass that can do it all? From short-stemmed to swirlable, dishwasher-friendly to delicate, here’s the glassware that’s a cut above the rest • The best no- and low-alcohol wines for when you’re off the booze It is a truth only sometimes acknowledged that wine is in want of a good drinking vessel. Why? Because wine experts agree that the shape, character and feel of a glass give wine the conditions to shine. “A good glass can greatly improve your experience,” writes David Williams in The Encyclopedia of Wine . He adds that expense isn’t necessary: “[A]s a rule, the thinner the glass the better, while an oval shape and generous (but not enormous) bowl are best at capturing and releasing a wine’s flavours.” Drinking wine is an experience beyond flavour; before the taste, there is the nose, and a good glass will amplify its aromas. Likewise, there is the ineffable question of how a wine makes us feel; again, your choice of glass feeds into this experience – how does it feel to hold, to swirl, to sip from? Continue reading...

articles.title: A Robbie Williams film starring a CGI chimp helped me come to terms with my hearing loss
articles.description: I was bullied for my deafness as a child, and just when I was finding myself, a car crash set me back years. But then I watched the movie Better Man, and had my life explained for me I cannot say I’ve ever been a Robbie Williams fan. When I went to see Better Man, the 2024 biopic in which Williams is played by a CGI chimp, I was tagging along with my wife. To be honest, I was sceptical about the ape but tried to meet the film with an open mind. I wasn’t looking for anything in particular but what I found was something that seemed to explain my life. I was born two months premature in Winnipeg, Canada, in 1961, with severe hearing loss in both ears that wasn’t diagnosed until I was seven. In 1969 we moved to Woking in Surrey; my father left and my mother descended into alcoholism. I was a misfit in my family, with no support for my deafness, and at school the bullying – from kids and teachers – was something awful. In my desperate isolation, I turned to reading: book reading, lip-reading, and reading the room. Forget TV, forget music – the Beano and Beezer were my survival manuals: the Numskulls taught me how my brain worked with broken ears. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘The spirit of a borderless Europe steams from the pots and pans of Vienna’
articles.description: There’s more to the Austrian capital’s cuisine than schnitzel – its dishes come from all over the world The Viennese love to eat. That isn’t solely a sign of joie de vivre. Sometimes it’s just hunger. The city has a long history of decline. Entire empires have crumbled here, or simply dissolved. Emperors took a final sigh and slipped under the table, ministers burst while tucking into their dessert, poets quietly starved to death or choked on their own self-importance. Vienna’s cuisine has outlasted them all: a little bit too heavy, a bit too greasy, and always covered in breadcrumbs or sprinkles. Consider the schnitzel, for example. The Wiener Schnitzel is a legend, supposedly a dish of world-class stature: golden-yellow and wavy, spilling over the plate, with a delicate wedge of lemon daintily nestled beside it (in some of the more upmarket establishments, it even comes wrapped in a little linen pouch). There are few dishes that are so passionately raved about while being so fervently disparaged. articles.title: Why I won’t leave mathematics, despite AI solving centuries-old problems | Ken Ono
articles.description: I believe human judgment remains essential Last year, I nearly quit mathematics. On 20 November, Levent Alpöge announced that, working with Claude, he had proved the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old problem about the distribution of prime numbers. The Lean and Mathlib communities have since certified the formal proof. We are only beginning to understand the argument. What kind of future awaits someone beginning a life in mathematics? In May 2025, I led the number theory team for Epoch AI’s FrontierMath project. We wrote difficult problems to test large language models. I watched an unreleased ChatGPT model compute all the moments of Tamagawa numbers of elliptic curves, drawing on work by Manjul Bhargava and Roger Heath-Brown, and on papers my father wrote in the 1960s. I was stunned. Ken Ono is a number theorist and professor of mathematics at the University of Virginia, currently on leave as founding mathematician at Axiom Math. They even, on occasion, fail to tell the truth despite having sworn to do so – in court, for instance, or staring deeply into the eyes of someone who is sitting right there . Is that a shock? articles.description: Illinois Reveals Attempted Dam Cyberattack Days After DNI Swore "This Is Not A Cyberattack" Illinois' Department of Natural Resources said Friday that someone made an apparent cyberattack attempt on the Algonquin Dam on the Fox River on Monday, the same day a string of outages hit major US banks, and two days before the White House insisted the week's tech failures were not an attack. Illinois officials say the Algonquin Dam remained fully operational after staff detected an apparent cyberattack attempt on Nov. 16. Illustration featuring Jay Clayton and the Fox River spillway. The dam sits in McHenry County, about 45 miles northwest of Chicago. IDNR's Office of Water Resources, which operates it, spotted the attempt, and staff "took immediate action to keep the dam secure and fully operational," the department said, according to the Daily Herald . IDNR said it has no indication the incident is tied to other recent cyber events. Illinois State Police, the Illinois Emergency Management Agency, the Illinois Department of Innovation and Technology and the federal Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) are investigating.
